BiblicalUsage: The word means to knead, the ordinary work of hands in dough, and it appears at both holy and shameful tables. Sarah kneaded cakes for the three visitors at Abraham's tent, and Tamar kneaded cakes in her brother Amnon's sight before he seized her. Jeremiah shows whole families kneading dough for cakes to the queen of heaven, and Hosea pictures adulterers as an oven heated by the baker after he has kneaded the dough.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe kneading shows how the same hands can serve God or serve idols, and the difference is not the work but the worship. I hold that God sees the quiet work of the kitchen as clearly as the work of the temple, and He calls His people to knead for Him alone.
